prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1316; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver. Vehicles came to rest in the travel lane. Both drivers state no airbags deployed. Claimant reports headache and dizziness at the scene and was transported to a local hospital by ambulance. Photos requested from both parties and tow yard contacted for vehicle storage.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports being diagnosed with a concussion and is off work pending follow-up with their physician. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the claim directly. Explained the claims process, the difference between property damage and bodily injury coverage, and that medical records will be needed to evaluate the injury portion of the claim. Claimant agreed to sign medical authorization forms.

Entry 3: Received police report. Other driver cited for failure to yield at an intersection approach. Liability appears clear on the report. Reviewed both vehicles' damage estimates; repair totals are within expected range for a low-speed impact. Rental coverage confirmed for the claimant's vehicle. Sent medical authorization forms to claimant by mail and email.

Entry 4: Claimant returned signed authorization forms. Requested records from the treating clinic and emergency department. Claimant reports ongoing light sensitivity and difficulty concentrating, and asked whether a settlement offer would be made before treatment concludes. Advised that the injury claim cannot be fully valued until treatment is complete and records are reviewed. Noted that claimant may wish to consult an attorney, and provided the state consumer insurance information guide.

Entry 5: Medical records received from emergency department and primary care clinic. Records confirm diagnosis of concussion with recommendation for rest and gradual return to activity. Follow-up scheduled with neurologist still pending. Claim file flagged for periodic status review. Next contact with claimant set for after the neurology appointment. Reserves reviewed and adjusted for the bodily injury component.
